claim.quote: Furthermore, we present a limit on the spin-independent dark-matter nucleon elastic scattering cross-section achieving a sensitivity of $\mathcal{O}$(pb) with an exposure of only 11.6 g d.

name: Deep-underground dark matter search with a COSINUS detector prototype
notes: Prototype result, not a COSINUS-1pi measurement.

summary.plain: The first underground test of a COSINUS sodium iodide cryogenic detector, a 3.67 g crystal at Gran Sasso, showed much better separation of electron events from nuclear recoils and set a dark matter limit with only 11.6 gram-days of data.
summary.technical: 3.67 g NaI absorber with remoTES read-out and an improved silicon light detector at LNGS: nuclear-recoil baseline resolution sigma = 441 eV (five-fold improvement) and a spin-independent limit with sensitivity O(pb) at 11.6 g d (Phys. Rev. D 110, 043010).

title: Deep-underground dark matter search with a COSINUS detector prototype
why_it_matters: The paper calls the cryogenic NaI read-out a promising route to a model-independent test of the DAMA/LIBRA signal.
